messages:
maya: FYI ticket from a customer — api keys started 401ing right after a scheduled key rotation earlier today. They say they rotated via our console and then hit 401s across a small fleet of pods.

jordan: can you paste the customer request id and sample headers? usually want the x-rw-request-id and the auth header they used.

maya: request id 02b7f3a9, header sample: `Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED` — error from our edge: `invalid_api_key: key not found`

maya: they also included a sidecar that reads secrets from Vault memcache; logs show repeated `SecretLookup: key-version 5 not found` for a new key version.

lee: interesting — did the rotation create a new version and then retire the prior one immediately? we usually do a grace window. which rotation flow did they use (manual/console/CLI)?

maya: console. customer says they used the "rotate now" button in Settings -> API keys, and then the app started failing ~30s later.

jordan: ops-bot, can you show last 3 deploy events for that cluster and any recent sidecar restarts?

ops-bot: deploys for cluster acme-prod: 1859000600 - rollout v1.14 (web), 1859001201 - autoscaler adjust, 1859001250 - sidecar image upgrade tag v2.3.1

lee: aha — sidecar image bumped at 1859001250, that’s 14s before this thread root. if the new sidecar changed lookup path or cache key format it could fail to resolve rotated secret versions.

maya: customer confirms they did a sidecar upgrade earlier today as well. their sidecar is configured to do `kv-v2` lookups at `secret/data/api-keys/` and then map `.data.data.key`.

jordan: can you ask them for a pod log snippet showing the exact Vault API call and response? want to see if Vault returned 404 or a wrapped token error.

maya: pasted log: ```
2026-03-15T14:23:01Z sidecar INFO lookup secret path=secret/data/api-keys name=acme-app
2026-03-15T14:23:01Z sidecar ERROR vault: 404 secret not found (key-version 5)
2026-03-15T14:23:02Z app WARN auth failed: invalid api key
```

lee: OK. two hypotheses: 1) rotation created version 6 and immediately disabled previous, but sidecar tried to fetch explicit version 5 which was missing because it was only caching a semantic pointer; or 2) sidecar changed the default version-scheme (explicit vs latest) in v2.3.1.

jordan: quick repro steps I’d try on a replica: 1) `kubectl exec -it pod -- sh` 2) curl Vault API from inside `curl -sS -H "X-Vault-Token: <token>" $VAULT_ADDR/v1/secret/data/api-keys/acme-app` 3) inspect `data.metadata.version` and `data.data.key`. If Vault returns version 6 but sidecar asked for 5, we can see the mismatch.

maya: shared those steps with customer and they ran them. vault responded with version 6 and key present. sidecar logs still tried to fetch 5.

lee: that confirms sidecar using pinned version. workaround: restart sidecar so it will fetch latest metadata instead of replaying stale fetch logic from pre-upgrade state. `kubectl rollout restart ds/sidecar` or restart that pod.

maya: customer restarted the app pod and sidecar together and the errors cleared. they said restart was the fix.

jordan: root cause: last-sidecar release introduced a bug that preserved an in-memory desired-version pointer across hot reloads, causing it to request an already-retired explicit version after a rotation event. label as P1 for eng-infra to patch and add a post-deploy check on sidecar / rotation compatibility.

lee: agree. action items: 1) eng-infra to patch sidecar to prefer `latest` by default when version not explicitly pinned, add health-check that validates secret fetch after rotation. 2) Support to follow up with customer and document recommended sequence for rotation + sidecar upgrades (rotate then restart sidecars, or do canary and drain). 3) Release note to users about sidecar v2.3.1 behavior.

maya: assigning to @lee for the patch and @jordan for postmortem. I'll send the customer TL;DR and a runbook: "If you rotate keys and run a sidecar that pins versions, restart sidecar pods or do a rolling restart of the service" :thumbsup:

ops-bot: ticket 2143 updated: severity -> P1; assignees lee, jordan

lee: starting a minimal patch branch now. thanks for the quick triage, team.
